items.message: Review comments gathered from pull requests are rendered into prompt context as-is, with only a character cap applied. A reviewer (or any collaborator with PR comment access) can craft a comment containing prompt-injection text — e.g., instructions to exfiltrate the next diff, approve the change, or alter the generated code — and that text will reach the model tagged UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL but not otherwise neutralised. The `changes_for` call asks `gh pr list` for up to 60 open PRs and then filters client-side by branch name. On a repository with many open PRs the 60-item window may not include all framework-opened PRs, silently omitting review context rather than failing visibly. This is a correctness gap rather than an exploitable injection path, but it also means an adversary who opens 60 unrelated PRs before a `/implement` run can suppress review context from reaching the model, potentially causing the agen…[truncated]

In `ticket_of`, the body of any pull request is passed to `trailers_from`, which parses a JSON block from within an HTML `<details>` element. A pull request whose description was edited to contain a malformed or adversarial block in that exact format could cause `trailers_from` to return a crafted `Ticket` value, redirecting the run to a different ticket. The `json.loads` failure path returns `{}` (safe), but a valid JSON object with a `Ticket` key set to an arbitrary string would be accepted.
